## The Problem: Girls Enrol, but Don't Find Work {.smaller}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
![](../outputs/figures/d1_overall_gap.png){fig-align="center" width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}

```{=latex}
\vspace{0.5cm}
\begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.6em}
\item Girls' enrolment (\textbf{40.2\%}) exceeds boys' (\textbf{34.8\%}).
\item Yet girls' NEET (\textbf{46.8\%}) is nearly \textbf{double} boys' (26.4\%).
\item Nepal's gender gap is not a school-access problem — it is a \textbf{labour-market} problem.
\item Marriage explains more variation in girls' NEET than poverty, caste, and disability \textit{combined}.
\end{itemize}
```

:::
:::

## The Evidence: Education Reduces Exclusion {.smaller}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
![](../outputs/figures/m1_mincer_lifetime.png){fig-align="center" width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}

```{=latex}
\vspace{0.4cm}
\begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.6em}
\item Completing secondary school is associated with a \textbf{$-$13.2 pp} reduction in NEET probability (causal forest, $n=13{,}586$).
\item Each year of schooling: \textbf{+14.5\% earnings for girls} vs +12.0\% for boys.
\item \textbf{Beyond secondary} the gap widens: $\sim$+15\% per year for girls vs $\sim$+10\% for boys.
\item Effect is stable across all 7 provinces and all caste groups.
\end{itemize}
```

:::
:::

## The Cost: NPR 8 Billion per Cohort {.smaller}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
![](../outputs/figures/c3_coi_vs_budget.png){fig-align="center" width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}

```{=latex}
\vspace{0.4cm}
\begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.6em}
\item \textbf{NPR 8 billion (USD 61M)} is the lifetime productivity loss from one cohort of 680,000 adolescent girls not completing secondary education.
\item Equivalent to \textbf{$\sim$10\% of the annual health-sector budget}.
\item A \textit{new cohort enters every year} — this is a recurring, not one-off, loss.
\item Break-even: any programme costing under \textbf{USD 90 per girl} lifetime yields positive ROI.
\end{itemize}
```

:::
:::

## The Recommendation: Invest at 16–18, Not 19+ {.smaller}

```{=latex}
\begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.7em}
\item[\textbf{1.}] \textbf{End child marriage as an economic priority.} Marriage is associated with $-$61 pp enrolment and $+$42 pp NEET — the largest single lever. Enforcement of existing legislation in Madhesh and Lumbini would yield the greatest gain.
\item[\textbf{2.}] \textbf{Universal secondary completion with year-by-year retention.} 14.5\% earnings premium per year of schooling. Reward \textit{every year retained}, not only the completion milestone.
\item[\textbf{3.}] \textbf{Prevent the post-18 divergence — invest at ages 16--18.} The female NEET gap widens from $+$9 pp at 15--18 to $+$24.7 pp at 19--24. Retention support during upper-secondary, paired with skills bridges to the labour market and tertiary, is needed \textit{before} girls exit the system.
\item[\textbf{4.}] \textbf{Dalit-specific labour-market measures.} Education alone is associated with a 2 pp residual disadvantage. Pair education with apprenticeships and anti-discrimination measures.
\end{itemize}
```
